query:
The family had their regular Sunday video call. What did one family member's participation reveal about their actual relationship to the call — and what in Adaeze's account of the call makes that visible?

Options:
A. Kayode
B. Bisi
C. Emeka
D. Nkem
context:
[1] (about=Adaeze, episodic, t7 @2025-02-03T19:30:00) Good evening my children. Kayode, you have been on every call this month. I notice these things. God willing this continues.
[2] (about=Adaeze, episodic, t8 @2025-02-03T20:08:00) Nkem you are family. Anyone who loves each other enough to come despite finding it difficult - that is what counts. God willing you will feel more at home each time.
[3] (about=Auntie Grace, episodic, t6 @2025-01-27T17:41:00) My dear Emeka, please listen to Tolu. I see too many patients who push through when they should be resting 🙏 a missed Sunday is fine, just rest
[4] (about=Kayode, said_by=Tolu, profile, t8 @2025-02-03T19:32:00) Tolu notes consistency is the only thing the family chat requires.
[5] (about=Nkem, core, t6 @2025-01-27T17:02:00) Thinks missing church is natural after a full day; asks if Sunday call happened.
[6] (about=Seun, episodic, t8 @2025-02-03T19:57:00) Nkem I love that you said that honestly I mean you are allowed to find it a lot, no one expects you to perform being fine with ten people in one room
[7] (about=Uncle Dele, episodic, t12 @2025-02-17T20:05:00) ADAEZE correct. Christmas is at the family home. No variations required. Best regards, Dele
agent_answer:
D. Nkem

Nkem’s participation reveals that she finds the Sunday video call difficult—she is overwhelmed by a large gathering—but she still joins anyway. Her actual relationship to the call is that she comes out of love/family commitment despite the discomfort.

This is made visible in Adaeze’s account:

> “Anyone who loves each other enough to come despite finding it difficult - that is what counts.”
